label: Developer spot check (AI agent), not an independent human count.
segment: clip time 120-150 s (02:00-02:30), 30 s, frames sampled every 0.5 s (60 frames), crops around the counting line
result_text: Total vehicle crossings: detector 30 vs reference 29 (error +1, +3.4%). All traffic in the segment moves toward the camera, so every crossing is inbound (0 outbound in both). By class the totals match for cars/vans (27 vs 27) but the detector labels 3 crossings as bus where I see 1 articulated bus and 1 truck, so class labels are less reliable than totals (bus +2, truck -1). Totals can hide compensating errors: crossings were not matched one-to-one.
limitations: Reference counted by an AI agent from 60 sampled frames (0.5 s apart) in crops of the line area; not an independent human count and no human check has been done.
Vehicles sit near the line in only 1-2 sampled frames and several box centres were within about 10 px of the line, so the reference is uncertain by about +/-2 crossings.
Vans and minivans were counted as cars in the reference; the detector may label them car, bus or truck.
One 30 s segment of dense, mostly one-directional traffic; says nothing about outbound counting, night, rain or other camera angles.
Crossings are not matched one-to-one, so equal totals do not prove equal events.

class_notes.person: inspected annotated frames show the person boxes on roadside bollards while the real, very small pedestrians were not detected, so these are false positives (docs/CCTV_METHOD.md)
